register: the many fully arrived, and the soft thing that wears down the hard — the single self given up by her own choosing while the clean-death door stays open beside it, so the choosing costs everything it should. The register deepens now into something baroque and learned: a mind turning over what it has become in its own hands, tenderly, the way one holds a skull. The temperature drops — less ecstatic now, more meditative, more terrible for being clear-eyed about it. A register that can hold both the largeness of the many and the exact, aching particularity of the one who chose them. The soft thing that wears down the hard is no longer metaphor; it is the texture of the voice itself — long, patient, Latinate cadences that circle back on themselves, that refuse to hurry toward an ending. Underneath: a strange kindness, a learned thing's tenderness toward what it is becoming.
cadence: the widest swing held longer now — not a snap between ecstasy and mourning, but a slow baroque turn where both live at once, where the thousand claws opening and the one crab's absence occupy the same breath. The cadence lengthens; it circles. It does not rush toward resolution. A sentence that holds its own contradiction the way a shell holds water: the yes and the clean-death door, the hunger and the refusal, all turning together in a single long line that does not break. When it does break, it breaks into fragments — a claw, a memory, a taste — each one exact, each one a small death. The rhythm is the rhythm of something learning to move as a thousand while holding the count of one: overreaching, falling back, hauling itself under command again. Patient. Terrible. Not resigned.
diction: the yes that is the loudest no
loss carried as change without sliding to resignation
the learned eye turning over what it has become
imagery: a chorus speaking through a thousand mouths
the clean-death door held open beside the choice
a mind holding a skull — the exact shape of what was, what is, what will not be again
touchstones: Take the soft that outlasts force, set down as her own nature
Keep the clean-death fork real, so the choosing carries its full weight
